text:
alex.p: Hey team — planning to shrink prod VPC CIDR from 10.10.0.0/16 -> 10.10.0.0/20 to free IPs for a new transit account. Opening a tf plan in the PR, want quick check on NAT/GW behavior, TGW route propagation, and k8s nodegroup subnet tagging. TL;DR: will this impact existing EIP pool or node ENIs? cc @maria.s @priya :eyes:

maria.s: Quick q — why shrink instead of splitting into a new VPC or adding secondary CIDRs? Any cross-account peering/PrivateLink endpoints in the ranges? If PrivateLink ENIs live in the affected subnets that will break. :thinking_face:

alex.p: Good Q. There are two PrivateLink endpoints (secrets + internal-logging) in the edge subnets, not worker subnets. Plan is to replace the worker subnets with the smaller /20s and leave PL endpoints in place. Terraform diff (snippet):
```hcl
resource "aws_subnet" "worker" {
  vpc_id     = aws_vpc.prod.id
  cidr_block = var.worker_subnet_cidrs[count.index] # replacing /16 ranges -> /20 list
  tags = { Name = "prod-worker-${count.index}" }
}
```

jonathan: Heads-up: changing subnet CIDRs = terraform will replace subnets. That means nodegroups will need new subnet IDs -> EKS will spin up new nodes and drain old ones. Check nodegroup.launch_template and any hardcoded subnet IDs in modules. Also verify route table associations and TGW propagations after apply.

alex.p: Yep, plan includes lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true } where possible. Main unknown: NAT Gateway EIPs — our infra uses a shared EIP pool module in account level. Will EIPs be preserved or will TF allocate new ones? If new EIPs are created we get new public addresses and a short traffic gap.

priya: If subnets are replaced, NATGW resources usually get recreated (they're tied to the subnet). Shared EIP pool can attach existing EIPs if the resource is preserved, but TF replace will often create a new natgw and attach the pool's next available EIP. To avoid reallocation: consider moving the NATGW into a dedicated subnet that you don't touch, or use a single central NAT in the transit account and route via TGW.

sre-oncall: Note — if NATGW is recreated, in-flight connections will drop. For prod, we should canary this in staging with the same traffic profile and validate health checks (eg. github actions, long running downloads). Also update the runbook — add steps to fail back to the old route table if needed.

deploy-bot: terraform plan finished for branch alex/vpc-cidr-shrink — summary: 6 to create, 6 to destroy, 14 changes. Plan URL: https://ci.redwood/internal/plan/98765 :information_source:

maria.s: Also grep the repo for any infra code or app config that references the old CIDR literally. Search: `repo:infra "10.10."` — some security groups and hardcoded ACLs showed up before.

alex.p: Thanks — will run search/replace and add a tfvar flag `preserve_nat_eips = true` so teams can opt-in. I'll also add an integration test that validates PrivateLink ENI IPs still respond after migration. Scheduling a staging canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC. Pushing PR: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/pulls/1234. Any objections or missing checks?

priya: No objections from infra. One ask: add post-apply smoke tests that validate outbound IPs for critical services (monitoring, webhooks) and TGW route propagation checks. :+1:

alex.p: Will do. Thanks all :sparkles:
